strings.name: Meg Whitman
strings.role: Albertsons executive chair and former U.S. ambassador to Kenya
strings.summary: Meg Whitman is an American executive and former diplomat who led eBay, Hewlett-Packard and HPE, then served as Quibi CEO and U.S. ambassador to Kenya. Her career includes platform growth, corporate restructuring and an unsuccessful startup. She became Albertsons executive chair in 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. HP and HPE, CEO and chair, and confirmation and diplomatic tenure are distinguished. Quibi’s wind-down does not establish the same-day end of her corporate role.
strings.influence.rationale: Led eBay’s expansion and participated in HP’s transformation, influencing ecommerce platforms and large technology-company management.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Princeton economics bachelor’s, class of 1977; Harvard Business School MBA.
strings.facts.f2.label: Public service
strings.facts.f2.value: U.S. ambassador to Kenya from 2022 to 2024; Republican candidate for California governor in 2010, losing to Jerry Brown.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Platform and corporate leadership
strings.highlights.h1.text: Held leadership responsibilities during eBay’s expansion and HP’s restructuring; business results reflect collective organizational work.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Strategic decisions and setbacks
strings.highlights.h2.text: While leading Quibi, joined Jeffrey Katzenberg in acknowledging the venture’s failure and announcing its wind-down in 2020.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Becomes Albertsons executive chair
strings.timeline.t1.text: Takes the newly created role supporting CEO Susan Morris; Kim Fennebresque becomes lead independent director.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Returns to The Nature Conservancy board
strings.timeline.t2.text: Institutional biography records election to a new three-year term; her previous service ended in January 2020.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Confirmed as ambassador to Kenya
strings.timeline.t3.text: The Senate confirms her nomination en bloc by voice vote; confirmation differs from the oath or presentation of credentials.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Announces Quibi wind-down
strings.timeline.t4.text: Signs an open letter with Katzenberg announcing wind-down and efforts to sell content and technology assets.
strings.timeline.t5.title: HPE CEO handover
strings.timeline.t5.text: Antonio Neri takes over; the earlier announcement says Whitman will remain a director.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Becomes Hewlett-Packard CEO
strings.timeline.t6.text: Becomes president and CEO of the then Hewlett-Packard Company; later HP Inc. and HPE roles must be distinguished.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Hands over eBay CEO role
strings.timeline.t7.text: John Donahoe succeeds her; the contemporaneous announcement takes precedence over later claims of a November departure.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Joins eBay as president and CEO
strings.timeline.t8.text: Joins an existing company and advances its expansion; she is a hired leader, not eBay’s founder.
